short: In two sentences, explain what a cell tower does.
long:
The following passage describes how a mobile phone joins a cellular network. When a phone is switched on it scans the frequency bands it supports and looks for synchronization signals that base stations broadcast at regular intervals. These signals let the phone line up its clock with the cell and read a small block of system information that says which network the cell belongs to, how to request access, and which frequencies carry the rest of the configuration. Once the phone picks a cell it performs random access by sending a short preamble on a shared channel. The base station answers with a timing correction and a temporary identifier, and the phone uses that grant to send its first real message asking for a radio connection. After the radio connection is set up the phone talks to the core network rather than the tower. It identifies itself with a concealed version of its subscriber identity, and the core looks up the matching key to run a challenge and response exchange. Both sides derive fresh keys from that exchange, and from then on signaling is encrypted and integrity protected. The core then registers the phone in a tracking area so it can be paged later when data arrives. To actually send user traffic the phone asks for a session to a named data network. The session management function picks a user plane function to anchor the session, assigns the phone an address, and installs rules that tell the user plane how to forward packets and which quality of service to apply. The base station sets up a matching radio bearer, and packets from the phone travel over the air to the base station, through a tunnel to the user plane function, and out to the destination. Replies follow the same path in reverse. Throughout the session the base station schedules every transmission in small time slots, choosing modulation and coding based on reported channel quality, and retransmitting blocks that fail to decode. Higher layers add their own recovery, so a single lost block usually costs a few milliseconds while repeated losses can stall a transport connection for much longer.

Using only the passage above, summarize in three sentences what happens between switching on the phone and sending the first packet of user data.
